title: Final review of the Phase 4 diff
description:
Review the whole epic's diff against its definition of done, outside-in.

The phase's gate is project w1z A1 again: AN EPIC COMPLETES UNATTENDED AND MERGES ITS OWN PR, through the new reconciler, with a Workflow restart mid-run and every in-flight attempt reconciled from .ticfac/. That is not a checklist item to tick - it is a run to perform and watch. Phase 3's own retro says ticfac was not ready for it, so this review is where that verdict is re-taken with evidence.

Ask explicitly, because each is a way this phase passes on paper and fails in fact:
1. Did the epic complete with NO operator intervention? Count the holds and resumes. Phase 3 needed a person 11 times and called itself supervised; a phase that needs one person once has not met this gate.
2. Did the Workflow restart mid-run and recover every in-flight attempt from .ticfac/, or was the restart skipped because the run was going well?
3. Does the TypeScript tracker client agree with tk, proven against the pinned 3.2 fixtures rather than by inspection?
4. Is 9da actually fixed, or did the close-out merely happen to win the race this time? Move the PR head during a close-out and watch.
5. Did anything change the reconciler's SEMANTICS to fit the host? Those are decisions to record, not implementation details.
notes:
2026-09-18 16:11 - AMENDED (operator decision, 2026-09-18): the gate is no longer 'an epic completes unattended and merges its own PR'. It is 'an epic runs to completion unattended and stops at a PR that is REVIEWED and CI-VERIFIED, for a person to merge.'

Where the old wording came from: SPEC 12 Phase 4 says 'project w1z A1 again', and w1z's A1 reads 'An epic submitted with tk cloud run completes - waves, gates, merged PR - with the operator's laptop offline from submission onward.' The merge was never an independent decision; it fell out of 'laptop offline'. Nobody at a machine means nobody to merge.

Why it changed: the merge is the one step worth keeping a person in. Everything before it - the waves, the per-tick gates, the review, the close-out - is work a machine can prove it did. The merge is a judgement about whether to accept the work, and a PR that is reviewed and CI-verified is exactly the artefact a person needs to make it quickly.

So question 1 of this review changes: do not ask whether the run merged. Ask whether it reached a reviewed, CI-verified PR with no operator intervention, and COUNT the interventions. One is a failure. Merging is not one.

Two things this makes sharper rather than weaker:
- the review must actually be ON the PR. A verdict that exists only in the run's records is not a reviewed PR; the person merging has to read it where they merge.
- CI-verified means green on the head that would be merged, re-derived at close-out time. 9da's repair is what makes that honest when the run's own writes moved the head.

Note for whoever reconciles this upstream: SPEC 12 Phase 4 and ticks w1z A1 still say 'merged PR'. This repository's gate now disagrees deliberately. Amend the SPEC, or record there that ticfac's Phase 4 gate diverges and why.
